example_prompt: Receive and verify a KadevPay payment.success webhook event before fulfilling an order.

net_amount.description: Amount after KadevPay 3% fee in XOF

gotchas: Verify the signature: HMAC-SHA512 with KADEVPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, hex digest, compared with the x-kadevpay-signature header. Use SHA-512, not SHA-256. Whether the hash covers the raw request body or the parsed body re-serialized is not settled: KadevPay's own examples disagree (see open_questions). This example follows the Node.js one, JSON.stringify(req.body); if valid webhooks fail the check, compare with the raw body as the PHP and Python examples do.
Only act on event === 'payment.success' — other event types may be added by KadevPay in the future.
net_amount is the actual revenue after KadevPay's 3% fee — use it for accounting, not amount.
Always call verify_payment server-side after receiving the webhook — never fulfill based on the webhook payload alone.
Return HTTP 200 immediately; process the event asynchronously. The webhook URL must be HTTPS and configured in the KadevPay dashboard.
open_questions: What the signature covers: KadevPay's examples at https://pay.kadev.ci/developer-documentation (Webhooks > Vérification de la Signature) disagree. Node.js (Express) hashes the parsed body re-serialized: ".update(JSON.stringify(req.body))". PHP hashes the raw body: "$payload = file_get_contents('php://input');" then "hash_hmac('sha512', $payload, $webhook_secret)". Python (Flask) too: "# On récupère le payload brut" then "payload = request.get_data()". The two only agree if KadevPay sends the body exactly as JSON.stringify serializes it, which the docs do not say.

evidence.source_reference: Webhooks > Vérification de la Signature — PHP, Node.js (Express) and Python (Flask) tabs; the tab contents are served by the page's bundle https://pay.kadev.ci/assets/index-COQarm8F.js, which snapshot_hash covers
